newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks jump 7.99 pct shortly after open.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks jump 7.99 pct shortly after open.

text.p: For the third day in a row, Thai stocks soared at the opening on Friday as orders from foreign buyers following the baht's de facto devaluaion on Wednesday continued to lift the bourse, traders and analysts said.
The SET Index rose 49.47 points or 7.99 percent to 667.51 by 0302 GMT. The SET 50 gained 4.36 points, or 9.53 percent, to 50.09 in trade worth 1.2 billion baht.

A backlog of at the market orders saw most blue chips up their daily limit of 10 percent within minutes of opening for the third straight day and investors were again looking around the market for liquidity, traders said.
"People are looking for around for whatever they can again today," said a trader at a local broker.
The no-limits foreign board was begining to show evidence of profit taking and investors were begining to search for stocks with fundamental value, traders said.
"It's been completely mad but it has to come back to fundamentals eventually," said a trader at a European broker.
